stem: Two Massachusetts collaborating pharmacists each hold Department registration for the purpose of prescribing. One will prescribe only Schedule VI products under her agreement. The other will prescribe products in federally controlled schedules. Neither holds a DEA registration. What follows?

choices.text: Both are barred, because the regulation requires DEA registration of prescribers.
Neither is barred, because Department registration is the operative requirement.
The first may prescribe; the second needs DEA registration because it applies.
The second may prescribe; the first needs DEA registration for Schedule VI.
Both may prescribe, provided each notifies the DEA of the agreement's terms.

explanation.core_reasoning: The registration condition names the DEA limb as applying IF APPLICABLE, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300. Where the substances the pharmacist will prescribe are federally controlled the limb bites; where they are not, it does not. The conditional wording is doing real work and is not a formality.

choice_analysis.A: The federal limb is expressly conditional.
choice_analysis.B: The federal limb bites where the substances are federally controlled.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: applicability turns on what will be prescribed.
choice_analysis.E: Notification is not a substitute for registration where it is required.

related_facts: Massachusetts Schedule VI has no federal counterpart schedule
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates read a conditional cross-reference as boilerplate and apply it uniformly or not at all.

reasoning_steps: Read the if applicable qualifier on the federal limb
Ask what each pharmacist will actually prescribe
Apply the limb only where the substances are federally controlled
